title: Should we keep checkboxes as default styling?
body: This is what the current default styling of the `refinementList` looks like: ![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/283419/10490683/a1fb2c26-72a2-11e5-922d-55c47d7e1bbb.png) And here is the current default template: ```html ``` I feel like using checkboxes for that is just one choice among many. What we really need is a way to tell which item is selected and which is not. Depending on the implementation, we could simply use bold text, or change the color, or add custom ✔ next to it, change its background, etc. For me this is something for the end-user to decide. I would then remove the `checkbox` from the default template and use a simple `Labelcount` instead, with a specific class added when the item is selected. That way, the user will be able to style it as needed (and we could also provide themes to help). It is possible to replicate a checkbox using CSS only (we actually do that on the current instantsearch demo). If users really needs a real `checkbox` in its markup, they can define a custom template. cc @Shipow @redox @andoche @kokliKo @vvo @proudlygeek @seafoox
